_comment: Single source for the simulator cards and scenarios. The "expect" blocks are written by the Go test (go test -run TestSiteScenarios -update-site .) and checked by it and by site/check-scenarios.js.

cards.title: Event dated next year
offer redeemed, expiry equals signed time
renewal signed at the refund time
status change with a revocation date
renewal of a new transaction, same expiry as the chain
renewal of the refunded transaction, signed after the refund

scenarios.name: Normal life
scenarios.note: Subscribe, renew, renew. Each message moves the version up by one.

scenarios.name: The store sends it twice
scenarios.note: The second DID_RENEW has the same notification ID, so nothing changes.

scenarios.name: Messages out of order
scenarios.note: The March renewal arrives before the February one. February is older than what is stored.

scenarios.name: Refund, then a bookkeeping message
scenarios.note: After a refund, switching auto-renew off must not give access back. Only a reversal does.

scenarios.name: A forged refund
scenarios.note: The forged message is rejected before it is even read. The user keeps access.

scenarios.name: Refund of an old renewal
scenarios.note: Refunding the February renewal does not end a chain that already runs to April. The refund is recorded against that one transaction.

scenarios.name: A refund before the renewal it does not concern
scenarios.note: February is refunded first, which ends the chain. The March renewal then arrives, signed earlier than the refund, and brings it back because it is a different transaction.

scenarios.name: Google upgrade, then a late message
scenarios.note: Token B closes token A. A late token A event is stale.

scenarios.name: The database blips
scenarios.note: While the database is down the answer is 500 and nothing is recorded, so the retry works.

scenarios.name: every Apple card in tray order
every Google card in tray order
two events signed at the same time
active event signed at the refund time
